title: Bolivia altitude ladder
note: Heights are approximate and rounded; towns spread over a range of heights. Every figure is listed in FACTS-TO-VERIFY.md.

stops.name: Nevado Sajama (summit)
stops.note: Bolivia's highest mountain. Expedition climbing only.

stops.name: Illimani (summit)
stops.note: The mountain on La Paz's skyline. Technical expedition climb.

stops.name: Huayna Potosí (summit)
stops.note: Often climbed as a guided 2–3 day ascent from La Paz.

stops.name: Chacaltaya
stops.note: Day trip from La Paz by road to near the top.

stops.name: Sol de Mañana geyser field
stops.note: Usually the highest point of the 3-day Uyuni trip. Approximate: sources give roughly 4,800–5,000 m.

stops.name: La Cumbre (top of the Yungas road)
stops.note: Start point for most downhill bike trips. Approximate.

stops.name: Laguna Verde
stops.note: Near the Chilean border, below Licancabur volcano.

stops.name: Laguna Colorada
stops.note: Red lagoon with flamingos; lodges nearby are among the coldest overnight stops on the trip.

stops.name: Potosí
stops.note: One of the highest cities in the world.

stops.name: El Alto International Airport (LPB)
stops.note: Where most international visitors land.

stops.name: Tiwanaku
stops.note: UNESCO World Heritage archaeological site. Approximate height.

stops.name: Copacabana
stops.note: Base for Isla del Sol.

stops.name: Lake Titicaca (surface)
stops.note: The level varies by season and year.

stops.name: Oruro
stops.note: Northern end of the Uyuni rail line.

stops.name: Uyuni (town)
stops.note: Approximate.

stops.name: Salar de Uyuni
stops.note: The salt flat is almost perfectly level.

stops.name: La Paz (city centre)
stops.note: The city spans roughly 3,200 m in the south to over 4,000 m at the rim in El Alto.

stops.name: Tupiza
stops.note: Alternative start for Lípez trips. Approximate.

stops.name: Sucre
stops.note: Often used as a lower rest stop between high places.

stops.name: Cochabamba
stops.note: Approximate.

stops.name: Samaipata
stops.note: Town below the UNESCO-listed Fuerte de Samaipata. Approximate.

stops.name: Coroico
stops.note: Common end point of Yungas road trips.

stops.name: Santa Cruz de la Sierra
stops.note: Bolivia's largest city and a second international gateway (Viru Viru airport).

stops.name: Rurrenabaque
stops.note: Gateway to Madidi and the pampas. Approximate.

advice.text: Altitude illness is unlikely at these heights. Santa Cruz, Samaipata, Coroico and the Amazon are good places to start or finish a trip.
Acute mountain sickness becomes possible, especially if you arrive quickly. Sucre and Cochabamba sit in this band and make useful stepping stones.

Once above about 3,000 m, clinical guidelines advise raising your sleeping altitude by no more than about 500 m a day and taking a rest day every three to four days. Flying straight into La Paz breaks this rule by design, so plan two or three easy days on arrival before going higher.
Acetazolamide can help prevent acute mountain sickness when a gradual ascent is not possible. It is a prescription medicine: discuss it with a doctor or travel clinic before you go.

Headache with nausea, dizziness or poor sleep is common mountain sickness: stop going up until it passes. Confusion, clumsiness, breathlessness at rest or a wet cough can mean high-altitude cerebral or pulmonary oedema, which are emergencies: descend and get medical help.
